title: Mechanical Systems: Gears and Pulleys
summary: Driver and driven gears, gear ratios, speed and direction of rotation, idler gears, chains and sprockets, belt drives and pulleys.

notes.text: **Gears** are wheels with teeth that mesh (fit together) to transfer rotary motion from one shaft to another. The gear that is turned by the motor or by hand is the **driver gear**; the gear it turns is the **driven gear**.

items: Two meshing gears turn in **opposite directions**.
A small driver turning a large driven gear: the output turns **slower** but with **more force** (torque).
A large driver turning a small driven gear: the output turns **faster** but with **less force**.

notes.latex: \text{gear ratio} = \frac{\text{number of teeth on driven gear}}{\text{number of teeth on driver gear}}

notes.title: Calculating a gear ratio
notes.problem: A driver gear with 15 teeth turns a driven gear with 45 teeth. (a) Calculate the gear ratio. (b) If the driver turns at 90 revolutions per minute (r/min), how fast does the driven gear turn?
steps: The driver turns 3 times for every 1 turn of the driven gear.

notes.latex: \text{driven speed} = \text{driver speed} \times \frac{\text{teeth on driver}}{\text{teeth on driven}}

notes.text: Idler gears and types of gears
An **idler gear** placed between the driver and driven gears makes the driven gear turn in the **same direction** as the driver. It does not change the speed.

rows: Simple gears on parallel shafts (clocks, toys)
Change the direction of rotation through 90° (hand drill, egg beater)
Change rotary motion into linear (straight-line) motion (car steering, sliding gates)
Large speed reduction; turns in one direction only (guitar tuning pegs)

notes.text: A **bicycle** uses a **chain** to connect two toothed wheels called **sprockets**. Unlike meshing gears, both sprockets turn in the **same direction**. A large front sprocket (chainring) driving a small rear sprocket makes the wheel turn faster.
A **belt drive** uses a rubber belt around two **pulleys**. It is quiet, cheap and flexible, but the belt can **slip**. Pulleys turn in the same direction unless the belt is crossed.

notes.latex: \text{velocity ratio} = \frac{\text{diameter of driven pulley}}{\text{diameter of driver pulley}}

notes.text: **Lifting pulleys** (as on a crane, a flagpole or a well) use a rope over a grooved wheel. A single fixed pulley changes the **direction** of the effort (you pull down to lift up). A system of several pulleys (a block and tackle) gives a **mechanical advantage**, so heavy loads can be lifted with less effort.

questions.prompt: A driver gear has 20 teeth and the driven gear has 60 teeth. Calculate the gear ratio (write the first number of the ratio only, e.g. 3 for 3 : 1).
A driver gear with 40 teeth turns at 60 r/min and drives a gear with 10 teeth. Calculate the speed of the driven gear.
What is the gear placed between two gears so that they turn in the same direction called?
Which gear system changes rotary motion into straight-line motion?
The two sprockets on a bicycle chain turn in the same direction.
Match each mechanism to an example.
A small driver gear turns a large driven gear. What happens to the speed and the force of the output?
questions.memo:
✓ The output speed decreases (1)
✓ The output force (torque) increases (1)

questions.prompt: Give ONE advantage and ONE disadvantage of a belt drive compared with gears.
questions.memo:
✓ Advantage: quiet / cheap / can connect shafts far apart / acts as safety if jammed (1)
✓ Disadvantage: can slip / wears out / stretches (1)

questions.prompt: Explain how a single fixed pulley on a flagpole makes work easier.
questions.memo:
✓ It changes the direction of the effort (1)
✓ so you can pull down to raise the flag up (1)
